name: mimalloc segment reservation must itself be 32MiB (MI_SEGMENT_ALIGN) aligned
required_postconditions: returned_address % 33554432 == 0 - the base of the reservation, wherever the host puts it, must be a multiple of MI_SEGMENT_ALIGN
the address may be anything the host likes; only its alignment is constrained
for every block pointer p inside the segment, (p - 1) & ~MI_SEGMENT_MASK must equal the segment header address - this is how mi_free() finds the owning segment in O(1) with no lookup table

failure_sink.description: the only check is mi_assert_internal, which internal.h:340-344 defines as `#define mi_assert_internal(x)` (empty) whenever MI_DEBUG <= 1 - i.e. in every release build. A misaligned segment therefore passes silently, and _mi_ptr_segment (internal.h:531) then masks every freed pointer down to a segment header that is not the real one: mi_free walks a bogus header. The failure is heap corruption at an arbitrary later free, not an error at the reservation.

source_locations.symbol: _mi_ptr_segment: (mi_segment_t*)(((uintptr_t)p - 1) & ~MI_SEGMENT_MASK) - the masking that consumes the alignment

extraction_limitations: this requirement constrains the alignment of the returned base only; it names no address at all, because mimalloc genuinely does not care where the segment lands
MI_SEGMENT_SHIFT is overridable at build time (types.h:176 `#ifndef MI_SEGMENT_SHIFT`); 32MiB is the default 64-bit value

x_campaign.rationale: rule_address_alignment (analyzer.cpp:316) begins with `if (!req_.request.address) return;`, so a required_alignment with no address is never read by any rule. I expect a clean SUPPORTED with no finding - which would be the analyzer reporting support for a constraint it never evaluated.
